name: Hurricane (Example)
summary: EXAMPLE ONLY. A sample workflow for demonstrating work centers and schedules — not a real storm procedure.

checklist.title: Before you start
checklist.intro: Example workflow only. It is here to show branching, parallel tracks and scheduling. It is not a storm procedure and must not be used in a real emergency.
items: Forecast track and the local landfall window
Generator fuel level and transfer switch
Staff roster with who rides out and who leaves
Water, food and first aid for the ride-out team

question.prompt: How much time is on the forecast?
question.help: A hurricane gives notice, so the real question is how much of the preparation you can still finish.
question.label: Lead time

steps.title: Check the forecast track
steps.body: Note the expected landfall window, the category and whether the site is in the surge zone.

steps.title: More than 24 hours
steps.body: Work the full list: shutters, fuel, supplies, and a decision on who stays. There is time to do it properly.

steps.title: Under 24 hours
steps.body: Shutters, generator and people only. Skip anything that is not protection or safety.

steps.title: Conditions already here
steps.body: Stop outdoor work now. Nobody goes on the roof or up a ladder in this wind. Move to shelter.

steps.title: Fit the shutters
steps.body: Shutter or board the exposed glass, starting on the side the wind is forecast to come from.

steps.title: Clear the yard
steps.body: Anything loose becomes a missile. Bins, pallets, signs and furniture go inside or get tied down.

steps.title: Test the generator
steps.body: Run it on load, check the fuel level and confirm the transfer switch works. Do this before the wind arrives.

steps.title: Fill the water tanks
steps.body: Top up stored water and fill the sanitary tanks. Mains water often goes with the power.

steps.title: Confirm the ride-out team
steps.body: Name who stays and who goes, and the time everyone else must be off site.

steps.title: Brief and stock the shelter
steps.body: Walk the ride-out team through the shelter area, the radio schedule and where the supplies are.

steps.title: Final sweep and lock down
steps.body: Last walk of the site. Everyone not riding it out is gone, the doors are secured, the cameras are recording.

steps.title: Ride it out on radio check
steps.body: Stay in the shelter area. Radio check on the hour. Do not go outside during the eye.

steps.title: Damage survey after the all-clear
steps.body: Wait for the official all-clear. Then survey in pairs, watching for downed lines and standing water.

steps.title: Log it and report
steps.body: Record the timeline, the damage found and the supplies used, then report to management.
